name: Hairline tattoo

lead: A hairline tattoo, formally scalp micropigmentation (SMP), is a superficial cosmetic tattoo that mimics tiny hair follicles. It can recreate the look of a buzz cut on a bald scalp, add density to thinning areas, or draw in a hairline.
The Wikipedia article is a short stub that relies mostly on news and magazine sources, and no clinical trials were found.

paras: Pigment is deposited into the epidermis and upper dermis, typically over three to four sessions of about two hours, with ink matched to hair colour. A patch test for ink allergy may be done first.

The article names an unnatural result from poor hairline work and possible ink allergies as the main risks, and says there are no scientific data on long-term effects, with the treatment described as permanent but removable by laser.

lead: A hairline tattoo, more formally scalp micropigmentation (SMP) or hair tattoo, is a non-surgical, superficial cosmetic tattoo that creates the look of closely shaved hair on a bald scalp or adds apparent density to thinning areas [1]. It is also used to conceal hair transplant scars and other scars on the head [1].

The hairline is described as one of the most crucial parts of the treatment, and poor work can look unnatural, though hairlines can be adjusted or touched up relatively easily [1]. The Wikipedia article is a short stub, with several claims lacking citations and sources that are mainly news and magazine pieces [1].
infobox: Typically three to four of about two hours [1]
Described as permanent; removable by laser [1]

paras: Unlike traditional tattoos, SMP deposits pigment in the epidermis and upper dermis, in ink matched to the person's hair colour. Practitioners may patch test first for allergies [1].

The main risks mentioned are an unnatural finish from poor hairline work and possible ink allergies. The article states that there are no scientific data on long-term side effects when ink comes from a reputable distributor [1].
